V_i = ofCone (c_i '' F(v_i)) ⊆ S(k_i): v_i read in its support L_i = span F(v_i) through a basis c_i : L_i ≃ ℝ^{k_i+1}, for EVERY choice of bases; bases exist (exists_bases_supports); each V_i is open, convex, nonempty, of empty noyau, line-free (hyps4_lecture)

findings: No new refutation. The Corollary (benzecri1960_ch3.tex:623-626) is proved by its printed route (l.628-632) under the hypotheses already carried by Prop. 4 / Prop. 5: F(w) without a line (OQ-168, OQ-171) and w nonempty. The reduction 'on se ramène à une décomposition de w en somme de convexes contenus dans des variétés distinguées simples' needs, beyond T-bz-c3-simples-somme, that each summand v_i, read in its support, is itself a domain of Prop. 4 (open, empty noyau, no line) and that the Prop. 4 summands of w and of the v_i correspond; the paper leaves both implicit, both are proved here (hyps4_lecture, sommandeS_lecture).

Degenerate case w = ∅ (∅ is an open convex of empty noyau): a Déf. 5 sum of ∅ has some v_j = ∅ and the other v_i arbitrary convexes, so 'w balayable ⇒ les v_i le sont' fails there unless every convex is sweepable; argued, not formalized (no non-sweepable / non-homogeneous open is available in the library). Imprecise only, the reading w ≠ ∅ is Prop. 5's.
questions: « les v_i le sont »: v_i is not open in S(n); read as v_i in its support l_i = s(span F(v_i) − O) ≅ S(k_i) through a basis, Vᵢ = s(cᵢ(F(vᵢ))), for every basis (the conclusion does not depend on the basis).
« convexes »: Déf. 5 summands (F(v_i) convex); nonemptiness and the absence of lines in F(v_i) are derived from those of w, not assumed.

Inherited and OPEN: OQ-168 / OQ-171 (no line in F(w)). Whether the Corollary as printed (without it) holds is not settled here; the known counterexample to Prop. 4 (the open quarter of S(2)) is not a counterexample to the Corollary.

kb_proposals: Prop. 5 basis-free (Sphere.prop5_lecture, Chapter3/BalayableSommeCor): X sweepable/homogeneous iff for every simple s, Lecture s (sommandeS X s) P (∃ n, basis b, hB, P ⟨ofCone (b '' val⁻¹' A), hB⟩); the ⇐ direction just `choose`s the bases, since prop5_balayable_somme holds for every bases — no basis-independence (IsProjIso) lemma needed.

Simple distinguished subspaces transport along any linear equiv: simples (e '' W) = map e '' simples W (Sphere.simples_image; IsCompl via Disjoint/Codisjoint.map_orderIso (Submodule.orderIsoMapComap e), Minkowski sum via Set.image_add).

A Déf. 5 summand v_i, read in S(k_i) through c_i : span F(v_i) ≃ ℝ^{k_i+1}, satisfies Hyps4 (Sphere.hyps4_lecture): F(v_i) = π_i(F(w)) (F_summand_eq) and LinearMap.isOpenMap_of_finiteDimensional on c_i ∘ projectionOnto.

Pitfall: `set L := span F (v i)` when a hypothesis c : ↥(span F (v i)) ≃ₗ … is in context shadows c as c✝ and breaks every later term; write the span out. Likewise `rw [F_summand_eq]` on `↑u ∈ F (v i)` with u : ↥(span F (v i)) fails the motive; rewrite the membership with Set.ext_iff.1 h ↑u, or use congrArg (fun X => …) h.
